description: 1D terminal-class fast lane in DetectionEngine: a second high-priority bounded Channel<FusedTelemetryContext> drained with precedence so IsAttackClassTerminal events at >=0.85 confidence reach the response path without queuing behind the normal rule sweep. Scheduling-only change: all tier law, Tier2-never-acts, observe-until-chain, and the mandatory pre-action audit still run downstream in AdvancedResponseEngine.HandleAsync. In src/Sentinel.Core/DetectionEngine.cs; independent of FEAT-001.
steps: In e:\Gorstak\Sentinel\.worktrees\hips-phase1\src\Sentinel.Core\DetectionEngine.cs add a second field '_priorityChannel' = Channel.CreateBounded<FusedTelemetryContext>(new BoundedChannelOptions(<capacity>) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.DropOldest, SingleReader = true, SingleWriter = false }). Keep the existing _telemetryChannel and its DropOldest/saturation RecordTelemetryDropped behavior unchanged.

Add 'internal static bool ShouldFastLane(FusedTelemetryContext context, double minConfidence)': derive the candidate DetectionEvent-shaped signal from context.TriggeringEvent and return true ONLY when ResponsePolicy.IsAttackClassTerminal(candidate) is true AND candidate.Confidence >= minConfidence. If the triggering event cannot be mapped to a terminal-class rule name, return false. This is a pure scheduling hint - never an authorization decision.

In SubmitTelemetry, after RecordTelemetryReceived, route: if ShouldFastLane(context, ResponsePolicy.DefaultMinTier1Confidence) write to _priorityChannel.Writer.TryWrite(context); else keep the existing normal-lane write (including the saturation RecordTelemetryDropped check). Routing is mutually exclusive so an event enters exactly one lane (no double-processing; dedup is unchanged).

Refactor the per-context body of ProcessTelemetryQueueAsync into 'private async Task ProcessContextAsync(FusedTelemetryContext context, CancellationToken ct)' containing the existing reputation Task.Run offload AND the 'foreach (var rule in _rules)' sweep + ProcessDetectionAsync calls, so both lanes run identical processing.

Rewrite ProcessTelemetryQueueAsync to a single loop that awaits readability on EITHER channel (e.g. await Task.WhenAny of the two WaitToReadAsync, or a combined wait), then each iteration FIRST fully drains _priorityChannel.Reader via TryRead -> ProcessContextAsync, THEN reads a single item from _telemetryChannel.Reader via TryRead -> ProcessContextAsync, looping back to re-check priority first. Thread _cts.Token through. Preserve the existing OperationCanceledException/ObjectDisposedException/Exception handling and shutdown semantics.

Confirm no static mutable state is introduced (channels only) and the mandatory pre-action audit path is untouched (the fast lane still routes through ProcessDetectionAsync -> HandleDetectionEventAsync -> AdvancedResponseEngine.HandleAsync).
acceptance_criteria: New test file e:\Gorstak\Sentinel\.worktrees\hips-phase1\tests\Sentinel.Tests\FastLaneTests.cs - Test A: a Tier2 detection with an IsAttackClassTerminal-looking rule name yields ShouldFastLane == false, and when submitted through the engine (temp-dir QuarantineManager + JsonlEventLogger + NullLogger mocks per DetectionEngineTests/AdvancedResponseEngineTests) produces a LOG response and never a kill. Passes.

FastLaneTests Test B: a Tier1 terminal-class rule (e.g. 'CVE Class: Kernel Exploit Loader', pid > 4, confidence 0.90) with ResponsePolicy.IsAttackClassTerminal == true yields ShouldFastLane == true. Passes.
Existing DetectionEngineTests still pass (normal lane unaffected).
No static mutable state added; CancellationToken threaded; Tier2 never short-circuits to action.
findings: DONE in src/Sentinel.Core/DetectionEngine.cs. Added instance field _priorityChannel = Channel.CreateBounded<FusedTelemetryContext>(1_000){FullMode=DropOldest,SingleReader=true,SingleWriter=false} alongside the unchanged _telemetryChannel (10k DropOldest + its saturation RecordTelemetryDropped). Added internal static bool ShouldFastLane(FusedTelemetryContext,double): derives a DetectionEvent-shaped candidate from context.TriggeringEvent (RuleName=TriggeringEvent.Type, ProcessId/ProcessName preferring the fused context then the trigger, Confidence=1.0) and returns ResponsePolicy.IsAttackClassTerminal(candidate) && candidate.Confidence>=minConfidence; returns false when context/TriggeringEvent is null or Type is empty. SubmitTelemetry now routes mutually-exclusively: ShouldFastLane(ctx, ResponsePolicy.DefaultMinTier1Confidence) -> _priorityChannel.TryWrite + return; else the existing normal-lane saturation-check + _telemetryChannel.TryWrite (unchanged). Refactored the per-context body (reputation Task.Run offload + foreach(_rules) sweep -> ProcessDetectionAsync) into private async Task ProcessContextAsync(FusedTelemetryContext,CancellationToken ct); the inner 'var ct=_cts.Token' was removed since ct is now the threaded parameter. Rewrote ProcessTelemetryQueueAsync to a single loop (ct captured once from _cts.Token) that each iteration FULLY drains _priorityChannel via TryRead->ProcessContextAsync, THEN reads one item from _telemetryChannel via TryRead->ProcessContextAsync (continue to re-check priority first), then when both empty awaits Task.WhenAny(priority.WaitToReadAsync(ct), normal.WaitToReadAsync(ct)) and only exits when a wait returns false AND both Completion.IsCompleted; preserves OperationCanceledException/ObjectDisposedException/Exception handling + shutdown. NO static mutable state (channels only); ct threaded through the drain loop and the reputation offload; fast lane is scheduling-only and still flows ProcessDetectionAsync->HandleDetectionEventAsync->AdvancedResponseEngine.HandleAsync so ApplyTierLaw/Tier2-never-acts/observe-until-chain/LogAuditBeforeActionAsync all run unchanged. KEY DESIGN NOTE FOR FIXER: raw TelemetryEvent carries NO RuleName/Confidence (only Type/ProcessId/ProcessName), so ShouldFastLane maps TriggeringEvent.Type -> candidate RuleName and treats it at full confidence; the gate is therefore governed by IsAttackClassTerminal (which includes the PID<=4 exclusion) plus the minConfidence floor. If future telemetry types carry a real confidence/rule-name, extend ShouldFastLane's candidate derivation rather than the routing. Added tests/Sentinel.Tests/FastLaneTests.cs: ShouldFastLane_Tier1TerminalClass_ReturnsTrue (CVE Class: Kernel Exploit Loader, pid 4242 -> true), ShouldFastLane_PidTooLow_ReturnsFalse (pid 0 -> false), Tier2Lookalike_DoesNotFastLane_AndLogsNeverKills (civilian 'Reverse Shell: Suspicious Outbound Connection' -> ShouldFastLane false; submitted through engine yields ActionTaken:LOG and never KILL/QUARANTINE_AND_KILL for its PID), ShouldFastLane_NullOrEmptyTrigger_ReturnsFalse.
